chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a boy who was breast-fed by a woman: Is it permissible for him to marry her sister (who is related) by the father, through breast-feeding? He (peace be upon him) said: No, for they have both been breast-fed from the milk of one stallion (father), from one woman.

He (the narrator) said: So can he marry her sister (who is related) by the mother, through breast-feeding? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with that, for her sister, who did not breast-feed him, had a different stallion (husband) from the one who breast-fed the boy. So if the two stallions (fathers) are different, there is no problem.

key_terms.فَحْل: Stallion (metaphor for the father/husband in the context of milk lineage)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying the sister of a milk-sister when they share the same father but different mothers?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the juristic principle of 'fahl' (stallion) in Shia fiqh, where the father's milk is considered equivalent to the mother's for establishing kinship. It distinguishes between full milk kinship, which prohibits marriage, and partial kinship where differing fathers render the milk sources distinct, thereby permitting marriage. This reflects the scholarly consensus on how biological lineage through milk is traced to determine mahram relationships.
